sd_east_side_sd.blurb: East Side SD covers a handful of crags in pink Sioux quartzite near Sioux Falls. Palisades State Park, by Garretson, holds most of the climbing along the cliffs of Split Rock Creek, with top-rope and trad lines plus some bouldering. Friction is limited, so crimps, slopers and cracks do the work, and leaders should be confident placing gear. The Dells of the Sioux River, near Dell Rapids, is mostly sport, with some top-rope and bouldering, and Devils Gulch is a small canyon crag whose routes can be dirty. Routes run from easy scrambles to 5.12, with most between 5.7 and 5.10, and boulder problems span V0 to V5. Spring and fall are the most comfortable seasons, while summer is humid and buggy. One side of Palisades gets shade and the other gets sun.

co_central.blurb: Central is the middle section of the Flatirons, on the foothills west of Boulder, Colorado. The rock is hard conglomerate sandstone, and the area is a patchwork of many smaller slabs and formations rather than a few big walls. Trad is the largest group, followed by bouldering, then sport, with a little top-rope. Grades spread from easy scrambles through the full range up to 5.13, with a good number of climbs from 5.10 to 5.12, and boulder problems mostly between V0 and V9. Bear Canyon Bouldering, Der Zerkle, Finger Flatiron and Der Freischutz are among the biggest pieces. The sharp rock can bite, the setting is quiet and scenic with views into Bear Canyon, and the southwest faces catch afternoon sun.

oh_wayne_national_forest.blurb: Wayne National Forest in southeast Ohio is a sandstone bouldering destination. Most of the climbing is in the Marietta Unit, just north of Marietta, where boulder zones are scattered through the forest. The smaller Ironton Unit adds some sport, trad and top-rope routes around Lake Vesuvius. Boulder problems run from V0 into double digits, with most between V1 and V4 and a smaller group of harder lines. Rock quality ranges from very good to crumbly, and the sandstone is porous, so it needs a day or two to dry after heavy rain. Many lines are still unclimbed, so development is ongoing. Roped routes run from about 5.5 to 5.11.

ca_sherwin_plateau.blurb: Sherwin Plateau sits near Mammoth Lakes in the Eastern Sierra, at about 7,000 feet, on the edge of the Owens River Gorge. It is mainly a bouldering area on volcanic tuff, with a small sport wall on welded tuff. Problems lean easy to moderate, with a large number at V0, a solid spread through V3, and few above V5, though some taller highballs exist. Catacombs, Pocketopia and The Dreamers are the largest zones, and the pocketed tuff at Catacombs is not easy to find at first. Rimview Cliffs hold the sport routes, mostly 5.7 to 5.10, facing east with sun until early afternoon and views over the gorge.

ca_upper_gorge.blurb: Upper Gorge is the uppermost stretch of the Owens River Gorge, a steep canyon about ten miles long on the eastern edge of the Sierra Nevada. The river has cut through welded tuff, which gives edges, pockets and cracks, and most climbing is near-vertical. Sport dominates, with a smaller amount of trad. Grades run from 5.6 to 5.13, with some moderates, but the heart of the climbing is 5.10 through 5.12, so confident intermediate and strong sport climbers have the most to do. Lower Elbow Room, Dihedrals, Gotham City and Flavin Haven are among the larger sections. The gorge as a whole can be crowded, though walking farther usually brings quiet. It is climbable all year, although summers can be hot.

co_carbondale_area.blurb: Carbondale Area gathers climbing around the small town of Carbondale, below Mount Sopris, with Aspen about twenty minutes away. Climbing is split between sport and bouldering, with a smaller amount of trad and some ice. The Narrows, just south of town, has high-quality granite walls, mostly bolted, with technical face climbing and cracks from about 5.7 to 5.13, including a narrow slot-like section of water-polished rock. The Redstone area is mostly boulders with some sport, Coal Creek Boulders is almost all bouldering, and the Frying Pan mixes sport and trad. Sport grades cluster between 5.10 and 5.12, and boulder problems run from V0 to V10, mostly at the lower end.
